title: Compatibility offboarding and dependency mitigation roadmap
creator: Priya Nair
description: Run a staged, metrics-driven program to retire legacy compatibility layers for the /v1/compat API surface while minimizing disruption for customers that have indirect dependencies (SDKs, third-party wrappers, cached clients). This ticket coordinates launch planning, release-note sequencing, SDK and docs updates, customer outreach, and support runbooks. The goal is to provide clear upgrade paths, automated detection of at-risk customers, and safe fallbacks that allow the retirement to complete with <0.5% live-customer errors attributable to the change after 60 days.
goals: Publish comprehensive migration guides and SDK upgrade samples across JS/Python/Go
Ship changelog and per-customer transition timelines 8 weeks before final cutoff
Provide temporary compatibility gateway for tiered customers to reduce breakage
Automate detection and notify customers with client libraries older than supported versions
Coordinate support and engineering on rapid rollback and canary throttles
approach_summary: We will run an 8-week phased offboarding: announce + docs, SDK and infra updates, targeted customer outreach, canary deprecation window with telemetry gating, then hard decommission. Each phase has gating criteria tied to customer error-rate, upgrade uptake, and number of active legacy integrations. Cross-functional owners will own their artifacts and the PM will orchestrate deadlines and comms.

2025-03-24: Customer cohort identification and automated notification cadence set
2025-04-14: Deprecation start (non-blocking warnings in headers and logs)
2025-04-28: Canary enforcement window (5% traffic routed through strict checks)

comms_plan: Audience segmentation: public docs, existing customers, enterprise accounts, partners
Two-stage public comms: announcement (8 weeks) -> reminder (2 weeks) -> 72-hour final reminder
Direct emails to owners of accounts with legacy SDKs; SEs+AE alert for high-risk customers
Release notes: top-level summary, breaking changes section, migration checklist, code snippets
Console banners and API response headers with migration URLs during deprecation window
tasks: Docs: create step-by-step migration guide, code diffs, rollback examples
SDK: publish vX+ clients with deprecation warnings baked in; publish migration samples
Runtime/ENG: implement header warning 'X-Redwood-Compat: deprecated' and telemetry tag
Console/DX: show per-team migration status and countdown banners
Support: prepare triage runbook, canned responses, and escalation matrix
Legal/Compliance: review release notes and customer-facing language
Growth/Marketing: prepare blog post and changelog entry
Sales/AE: compile list of accounts with custom integrations and schedule outreach
acceptance_criteria: Migration docs and SDK samples live and linked from primary deprecation page
Automated detector correctly flags >=95% of customers using unsupported SDK versions
Canary enforcement passes with <1% unexpected 5xxs and rollback plan validated in staging
No P0 incidents resulting from decommission during the first 72 hours of enforcement
Support team has runbook and is staffed for the enforced cutoff window
monitoring_signals: Real-time: API 5xx rate for /v1/compat exceeding baseline by >2% triggers alert
Uptime SLA breaches for affected customers flagged to PagerDuty
SDK upgrade uptake: percent of active clients upgraded per week
Support ticket volume and time-to-first-response for migration-related issues
Console bouncebacks: number of customers who open migration docs after banner click
rollback_and_fallbacks: Feature-flagged compatibility gateway to quickly re-enable lenient parsing for affected tenants
Traffic rollback plan: shift canary % back to 0% within 15 minutes via routing policy
Emergency re-enable endpoint for enterprise customers with contractual requirements
Postmortem template and immediate measurement plan to identify root cause and next steps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: third-party SDKs repackage old clients -> Mitigation: partner outreach + automated detector
Risk: silent failures due to cached clients -> Mitigation: console banners + telemetry to surface client versions
Risk: legal/regulatory customers require longer runway -> Mitigation: account-level carve-outs and negotiated timelines
Risk: docs not discoverable -> Mitigation: link prominence in release notes, console, and SDK warnings
